text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A new round of proximity talks between the two sides start on Monday under United Nations auspices.
- A conflict of powers led to the resignation of the chairman of the church-controlled Hellenic Group of Companies.
- The Development Bank proposes turning Larnaca port into a cruise terminal.
- The United Nations embarks on an intensive round of contacts.
- Silent battle is underway for the control of shares in Vassiliko Cement.
- An indirect dialogue starts with British involvement.
- The archbishop comes under pressure to revoke his decision to sell Vassiliko shares to businessman Stavros Galatariotis.
- Rightwing Disy emerges from the crisis. Party elections are due to take place on May 18.
